title: The Dead Drop
subtitle: High Tech, Low Lives: Ann at the Harborview drop

beats.text: Three weeks since the feed went dark. You push through the door at 6:47, seven minutes early. Protocol: never be the last person at a dead drop.
Three weeks of g0's protocols: text in dead image files, orders that are not orders, cups that mean coordinates.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Learn this. Prove you can do it. Then we talk about the Blackout.
Today's protocol. Order a double espresso, no sugar. Set it at the corner table, handle to the window.
Check the cup three seats down. A stirrer across the rim means the message is live. Photograph it with your student ID in frame. Leave.
Simple. Except Manager Chen is already here.
Chen, from Applied Systems. Your lecturer on Tuesdays and Thursdays, who marks late arrivals in red.
She sits four tables away with a tablet and a cappuccino. You have never seen her anywhere before 8:55.
The dead drop cup is three seats from her. Handle at four o'clock. Stirrer across the rim. Live.

choices.ask: g0's file on you has one blank line. How do you work?

then.text: Your chrome hand whirs as the door closes behind you. Steel under the skin. You go through people and doors.

options.label: The Hacker
options.sub: The deck and the feed. Code +3.

then.text: The deck in your bag is warm against your hip. To you, every camera here is just another lock.

choices.ask: What do you take in first? Looking is free.

options.label: The cameras
options.sub: No dice, no time. Find where the feed is blind.

then.text: Three cameras. One dead seat, behind the espresso machine. The feed forgot it.
You keep your eyes on the menu board. You learn nothing. The feed learns nothing either.

options.label: Abort and sit with Chen
options.sub: Give up the drop. Hold on to your cover.

beats.text: You step to the counter. The barista's nails click on the register screen. She does not look up from her own feed.

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Double espresso, no sugar.
Your voice is steady. The machine hisses. You count four heartbeats. Now the register wants payment. Whatever you hand over, the feed will read.

then.text: 12 yen leaves your stipend. The transaction burns into the campus network with your name on it.
Coins on scratched steel. The barista does not look up. The name field stays black.
The reader chirps orange. It is AlgoCratic's own reader, and it reports its own badge.

beats.text: The barista slides the cup across scratched steel. You carry it to the corner table, the one with the peeling laminate. Handle to the window. Exactly to protocol.
Now the hard part. The cup you must check is three seats down. Chen is four tables away. She is reading, but she is *present*. One unnatural glance and she will remember.
Your chrome hand is faster than the camera's frame rate. Between two frames, a hand can do a lot.
The camera over the floor runs on the cafe's open network. Your deck can feed it six seconds of an empty seat.
You know the dead seat. It is on your way.

options.label: Palm the message past the camera

then.text: The chrome catches a chair back. The servos grind. Chen looks up, straight at you, with your hand halfway to your pocket.
You freeze. The photo is gone and the motion was wrong. You put the ID away like you were only checking it.
You drift past Chen's table like someone looking for a seat. Three steps. The chrome hand turns the ID and the phone together, faster than the frame. *Click.*
Cup, stirrer and timestamp. The camera saw a big shape walk by. That is all it saw.

options.label: Loop the camera for six seconds

then.text: The loop stutters. For half a second the feed shows two of you. Chen's tablet blinks, and she looks up, straight at you.
You freeze. No photo. You put the ID away like you were only checking it.
Six seconds of an empty seat play on CH 3. You walk through them. The ID comes up. *Click.*
Cup, stirrer and timestamp. The loop closes behind you without a seam.

options.label: Walk the blind line
options.sub: No roll. Needs the camera cones.

then.text: You cut behind the espresso machine, into the seat the cameras forgot. The ID comes up. *Click.* Cup, stirrer and timestamp.
No camera saw you take it. Chen did not look up.

beats.text: You sit. The espresso is bitter and cooling fast.
Chen gathers her tablet and coat. She stops at your table.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Ann. Didn't expect to see you here this early.

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Coffee before algorithms. Thought I'd try consciousness for once.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Admirable. You always sit in corners?
The question lands odd. Weighted.

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Better light. The window faces east.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Ann?

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Manager Chen. Hi. I was just looking for a seat.
Her eyes go from you to the cup with the stirrer across the rim, and back. She says nothing. She stays, reading but *present*.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: You seem distracted, Ann. If something is wrong, academically or otherwise, my office hours are Wednesdays.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Fatigue makes people careless. Careless people make mistakes they cannot take back.
It is an offer or a threat. You cannot tell which.
Your chrome hand ticks as it cools. Chen's eyes rest on it a moment too long.
In your bag the deck still hums. Her tablet sits on the cafe's open network, one hop away.

choices.ask: Chen is still in the room. Anything else?

then.speaker: ann
then.text: Is Thursday's exam on the whole term?

then.speaker: chen
then.text: On everything, Ann. It always is.

options.label: Ping her tablet with a fake alert

then.text: Her tablet buzzes. A campus alert, urgent and false. Her eyes drop to it and stay there. Your pulse is loud.

options.label: Rest the chrome hand on the table, between her and the cup

then.text: You set the chrome hand down flat. Now it is all the camera sees of the cup. The wrist servo grinds under the load.

beats.text: Chen is gone. The door chime rings once, and cold air follows it. Your phone vibrates on the table.
A dead image file. You decode it in three seconds.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Adequate. You completed the protocol under pressure.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Campus mailbox tomorrow, 4 PM. We talk about the Blackout then.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Mission failure. Chen is too observant and you were not ready.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: I am not burning you yet. Everyone fails a first live drop.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Debrief tomorrow, 4 PM, campus mailbox.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: You used the Harker badge. We will discuss the badge.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Cash. Old school. I approve.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Your hand is good. Do not let it make you loud.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Your deck is good. Do not let it make you forget that people have eyes.
The risk is too high. Chen is too observant, too present. You make the call in half a second. You walk to her table instead of the corner.

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Manager Chen. Mind if I sit?

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Ann. You're here early.

beats.speaker: ann
beats.text: Couldn't sleep. I thought coffee might help before Thursday's exam.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: Sit.
The dead drop cup stays three seats away, untouched. Protocol abandoned.
The talk is small: algorithms, the exam curve, the Harborview's burnt coffee. Chen's remarks about student stress are too precise for small talk.

beats.speaker: chen
beats.text: I should get to my office. Good luck Thursday, Ann.
The barista clears the dead drop cup ten minutes later. The window is closed.
The feed closes the day with one person unnamed, or named and forgotten. There is nothing to report.
You walk out into the early light. The mailbox is tomorrow, at four. Whatever g0 tells you about the Blackout, the feed will not hear it first.
The feed keeps the day. It is not a crime. It is a note.
The file carries the name Ann Sho, a student, seen at a cafe before class.
The file carries no name. It carries a face, and a time, and a cafe.
The file carries the name Sable Harker, an AlgoCratic employee, seen far from her desk.
Tomorrow, four o'clock, the campus mailbox. You will go. You will go the long way.
The drop is blown. The photo is missing. Chen saw you, and said what she said. g0 has not burned you.
Tomorrow you go to the mailbox and explain what went wrong. You will not enjoy it. You will learn from it.
You finish your coffee in silence, watching the trawlers cut through gray water. Your phone vibrates once.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: You aborted. Smart or cowardly? Hard to say.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: Chen is dangerous. You read that right. But I needed that confirmation.

beats.speaker: g0
beats.text: No second chances on this one. Maybe later. Maybe never.
If you want to see what happens when you take the risk, play again and proceed with the drop.
